summary:
The fix in MainWindow.ShowTopLevel works on the published single-file exe as well as in the in-process Facts. It records the selected and focused row Paths before the ItemsSource swap, reselects by Ordinal Path right after the swap, and refocuses the row in the Loaded callback when focus has come adrift.

**Real exe.** I ran the hook's top-key step 3 times against the published exe. Each run did a real scan of a 48,000-folder tree in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp and went through 3 live refreshes. After them:
- focus was on the 'reading' row's ListBoxItem;
- that row was selected and CanExecute was true;
- Ctrl+Enter went through the command's KeyGesture and reached that row's Path. The press ended in an injected-view refusal, so no Explorer window opened.

**Fix taken out (MainWindow reverted to 7bf476e, then restored byte-clean):**
- 24 of the 29 SL-100 Facts went red.
- The same exe step showed the bug itself: focus on the ListBox, focusPath and selectedPath null, CanExecute false, nothing revealed.
- With the fix restored, all 29 passed again and the exe was republished.

**All 14 design criteria are met by Facts that pass on net10.0-windows.**

**Required validate guards, all green:**
- SL-063: 10 of 10.
- Default suite: 804 of 805. The one red is AppArgumentTests. It flags the builder's untracked scratch launcher, .taad-scratch/sl100-topkey-run.ps1. With that file moved aside the class passes 3 of 3, so the committed tree is green.
- Fitness: 90 rules hold.
- Publish and L-001, L-002, L-003 (guard 5): all passed.
- WindowMutants -Mutant All (Q-114): all 12 mutants caught, 408 s.
- Rules harness, all scenarios (Q-026/Q-027, because fitness.yaml and ArchitectureRulesTests.cs changed): 124 of 124 rows AS-RECORDED. The run used the taad_v3 engine at e90d02b. The import rule is NOT RUN on the scratch copy, as always.

**Assumed scope.** The bug report was only a title. I took the scope to be Q-078, plus derived criteria 2-4, plus the half of SC-181 the loop can check.

**Not met, by decision.** Derived criteria 1 and 5 (containers kept alive; the Tag/CommandTarget pattern no longer needed) are not met, by the person's decision Q-078. Containers still detach on every refresh, so they are not built here.

**Left for a person.**
- R-001 step 16, which opens real Explorer windows.
- SC-181's by-hand clicks and an Alt+Tab with a real foreground switch.

**Temp folders.** My own temporary tree, hold folder and trx folder are deleted. 2 fsa-window-mutants and 16 fsa-window-cases folders remain in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp. I could not tell whether they came from my runs or were there before, so I left them.

checks.evidence: 804 of 805 passed in 26 s, exit 1. The one failure is AppArgumentTests.EveryScriptThatLaunchesTheAppIsListedAndQuotesByTheRule: 'Scripts that name or launch the app and are not in the corpus's producers: .taad-scratch/sl100-topkey-run.ps1'. That file is the build stage's untracked scratch launcher; it is not committed and will not merge. Scripts() also scans untracked folders, so any scratch launcher in a worktree turns the default suite red. Backlog: delete the scratch file before merge, or make the test skip .taad-scratch / gitignore it. The three LastAccess/HeldOpenTree reds that the doc says predate this slice did not appear in this run.

criteria.criterion: 1. Ctrl+Enter on the focused results row during a live scan, when the focused row is still being read and the tracker rebuilds it as a new TopLevelRow (the captured failure)
criteria.how: The repro Fact CtrlEnterOnTheFocusedRowStillWorksAfterTheLiveRefresh passes (unchanged apart from `partial`) and is red under M0. On the real published exe the top-key step passed 3 of 3: a reading row, 3 refreshes, focus and selection on it, CanExecute true, the press reaching its Path. The M0 exe showed focus on ListBox and CanExecute false.

criteria.criterion: 2. Ctrl+Enter when the focused row did not change (same object; its selection survives the Reset by itself)
3. Ctrl+Enter over three refreshes, where the rebuilt focused row grows past the largest and moves to index 0
criteria.how: FocusAndSelectionFollowARebuiltRowThatMovesToTheTop passes; it asserts SelectedIndex 1, then 0, then 0 and a press on the current object each time. Red under M0.

criteria.criterion: 4. Arrow keys after a refresh: Down on the restored row
criteria.how: ArrowKeysMoveOnFromTheRestoredRow passes; selection and focus move to 'gamma'. Red under M0.

criteria.criterion: 5. Keep my place: the focused row is below the first screenful and the list is scrolled
criteria.how: AScrolledFocusedRowKeepsFocusAndOffset passes: offset stays 30 and Ctrl+Enter reaches the row. Red under M0. A partly visible focused row may scroll by one row; that is not pinned and is filed as SC-264.

criteria.criterion: 6. Keep my place: a reorder pushes the focused row out of view, and a later refresh brings it back
criteria.how: ARowPushedOutOfViewStaysSelectedAndRegainsFocus passes. While out of view the row stays selected, focus stays on the list, there is no container and the offset stays 0. Once back in view it is refocused and Ctrl+Enter runs once. While it is out of view Ctrl+Enter is dead, which is the recorded, accepted gap.

criteria.criterion: 7. Focus on a control outside the list (the Cancel button) while a row is selected is never moved
criteria.how: FocusOutsideTheListIsNeverMoved uses the Settings button, because the Cancel panel is collapsed in the harness (m2, accepted). It asserts the button has focus before and after, and that the row is reselected. FocusThatMovesAwayBeforeTheRestoreRunsIsNotTakenBack covers focus moved in the gap. Both pass and are red under M0. FocusIsAdrift never matches a Button, so Cancel during a real scan is covered by the same branch, though not exercised.

criteria.criterion: 8. Nothing has keyboard focus (standing in for an inactive window): a refresh takes no focus
criteria.how: NoKeyboardFocusIsNeverTakenByARefresh passes. It builds a real inactive window, asserts IsActive false and FocusedElement null first, and checks that the refresh takes no focus but still reselects. Drift accepted under m7 / O-021: in an ACTIVE window with null focus the refresh now takes the focus (corpus F11), the opposite of the design's literal ClearFocus expectation.

criteria.criterion: 9. A row's ContextMenu is open when the refresh runs
criteria.how: AnOpenRowMenuSurvivesARefresh passes. The menu stays open, its entry runs once on the right row through Tag/CommandTarget, and after the menu closes and one more refresh runs, Ctrl+Enter reaches the row. Red under M0.

criteria.criterion: 10. ClearTopLevel or ShowFolderTree replaces the list between a tick's swap and its Loaded callback
criteria.how: ARestoreForAReplacedListDoesNothing passes: no dispatcher fault, ItemsSource and SelectedItem are null, no row has focus. The stale-array guard itself cannot be observed (mutant M3 survives, as declared).

criteria.criterion: 11. A key press queued at Input priority straight after the swap, before the restore runs
criteria.how: AKeyQueuedRightAfterTheSwapReachesTheRow passes on the real MainWindow, running exactly once on the rebuilt row, and is red under M0. A real hardware key in the gap is not measurable here (SC-254).

criteria.criterion: 12. Existing readers (revised marks, report, hook) enumerate TopLevelList.Items as TopLevelRow across live refreshes
criteria.how: TheListStillHoldsANewArrayOfTopLevelRowsPerRefresh passes. SL-063 passed 10 of 10. L-001 and L-002, which read the live list through the hook and the report, passed against the published exe. WindowMutants -Mutant All caught all 12 mutants.

criteria.criterion: 13. Cancel's ShowFinalTopLevel runs between a tick's swap and its Loaded callback, just after the focused row was rebuilt
criteria.how: AStopThatLandsBetweenTheSwapAndItsRestoreKeepsTheRowSelectedAndFocused passes: after settling, the rebuilt row is selected and focused. Red under M0.

criteria.criterion: 14. Two root children whose names differ only by case (a case-sensitive folder)
criteria.how: TwoRowsThatDifferOnlyByCaseKeepTheExactOneSelected passes, keeping the Ordinal match. Red under M0.

criteria.criterion: Merged SC-181: the same click-versus-refresh clicks pass against a net10.0-windows build of the app
criteria.how: What a machine can do here passed on net10.0-windows: the self-contained publish, and the top-key step 3 of 3 on the real exe. By hand: during a live scan of a large folder, click a row that is still being read, wait about 1 s (several refreshes), press Ctrl+Enter. Explorer must open with that folder selected. Then Alt+Tab away and back and press Ctrl+Enter again: it must open the selected row once the next refresh has run.

criteria.criterion: Q-078's window case: select a row mid-scan, wait for 3 refreshes, press Ctrl+Enter, expect a reveal (R-001 step 16)
criteria.how: Run `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case R-001`. Step 16 must log focusType ListBoxItem, focusPath = selectedPath = the row, canExecute true, and a reveal of that Path in a real Explorer window. The refusal-only variant of the same hook step ran unattended 3 of 3 here.

obligations.evidence: Under dispatcher ordering the cursor is re-derived before the next input. AKeyQueuedRightAfterTheSwapReachesTheRow puts a Ctrl+Enter at Input priority straight after the swap on the real MainWindow. It runs after the Loaded restore and executes once on the rebuilt row; it passes at HEAD and is red under M0 (MainWindow reverted). The reselect is now synchronous in ShowTopLevel, so SelectedItem is right before any input is processed. On the real exe, the top-key press after Flush reached the row 3 of 3. Not covered: a real hardware keystroke arriving in the swap-to-Loaded gap (SC-254).

In view, the re-derived row has a realised container. AScrolledFocusedRowKeepsFocusAndOffset (80 rows, scrolled to 30) passes, and so does the real exe top-key run (focusType ListBoxItem, 3 of 3). Out of view, it does not: ARowPushedOutOfViewStaysSelectedAndRegainsFocus measures no container (ContainerFromItem null). The row stays selected, focus stays on the list, and nothing scrolls. A later refresh that brings the row back refocuses it. That is the outcome the design accepts, so the precondition holds where it is relied on and its known exception is pinned.

not_reached: A real hardware Ctrl+Enter whose WM_KEYDOWN arrives between a tick's ItemsSource swap and its Loaded callback (SC-254). Every press here was raised in-process through the command's KeyGesture; this is not measurable on this machine.
A real Explorer reveal after the press (R-001 step 16). The exe runs ended in an injected-view refusal so that no Explorer window opened.

A real foreground switch: Alt+Tab, or Explorer taking the foreground and the app being re-activated. The Facts simulate activation within one thread (SetActiveWindow / SetFocus); a person's SC-181 run is needed.
A live scan of a real drive (C:\ or D:\) with a person scrolling and clicking. The exe ran only on a synthetic 48,000-empty-folder tree under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp.
Whether the restore scrolls by one row when the focused row sits partly visible in the viewport's last slot (SC-264). No test pins it, and I did not measure it.
Windows 10 and other DPI settings. Every run was on Windows 11 26200 at this PC's display settings; no Windows 10 machine exists here.
